text.p: A major shareholder of Sobieski Bancorp Inc said Monday it offered to buy the 89 percent of the thrift holding company that it did not already own for $18.20 a share.

Sobieski Chief Executive Officer Thomas Gruber said such a move would violate the South Bend, Indiana-based company's charter, which requires regulatory approval when any shareholder gains more than 10 percent of the company.
The stake held by the shareholder, Chicago-based Chiplease Inc, was pushed above 10 percent as a result of a recent stock repurchase by the company.
Chiplease Vice President Joe Treaber told Reuters that Sobieski management rebuffed Chiplease's offer, as well as its attempts to gain a seat on the thrift's board.
Sobieski Chief Executive Officer Thomas Gruber told Reuters that Sobieski made managment changes, planned to expand its loan line and bought back shares.
"We think we have a strategy in place to enhance shareholder value," he said in a telephone interview.

But Treaber argued that the thrift has produced poor results. Sobieski reported return on assets of 0.43 percent and return on equity of 2.34 percent for the fiscal year ended in June. That was down from return on assets of 0.74 percent and return on equity of 6.48 percent the previous year.
"Unfortunately, management has run the bank very poorly," Treaber said. "Expenses are way out of control."
Sobieski Chief Financial Officer Bill Smith said the decline in part reflected the thrift's transition to a public company, while a building program also impeded its financial performance.
Treaber also said Chiplease was opposed to the thrift's plan to expand into commercial lending.
"We're very much against this," he said. "We don't believe they have expertise to do this."
Treaber said Chiplease would seek to have Sobieski's charter converted to that of national bank at the company's next annual meeting, to be held in nine to 12 months.
Chiplease will also canvass shareholders to gain their approval for the takeover bid, Treaber said.
Sobieski shares were up 1-1/2 to 16-1/2 in afternoon trading on the Nasdaq.
